metais version — Print the tool's version and the specification versions it
implements.

Usage:
  metais version [--json]

Examples:
  metais version
      Prints the tool's version and the specification versions it implements.
  metais version --json
      Prints the same as one metais.version/1 document.

The tool's version is a semantic version. Its version is independent of the
specification's: a release may implement a new minor version of the
specification without a new major version of the tool. Every specification
version the tool implements is listed, ascending, so a caller tests membership
without knowing which minor versions imply which.

metais --version, before any command, is this command.

Flags:
  --json
      Print the result as one JSON document on standard output.
  --color <when>
      Colour human output: auto colours a stream that is a terminal when
      NO_COLOR is unset or empty; always and never override NO_COLOR. Values:
      auto, always, never. Default: auto.
  -h, --help
      Print help to standard output and exit 0; nothing else runs.

Prints:
  Two lines: metais and the tool's version, then the specification versions it
  implements. With --json, one metais.version/1 document.

Refusals:
  usage.bad_value
      A flag's value is missing, or is not one the flag accepts, or a flag that
      takes no value is given one.
      Next: metais version --help
  usage.repeated_flag
      A flag that may be given once is given again.
      Next: metais version --help
  usage.unexpected_operand
      An operand the command does not take.
      Next: metais version --help
  usage.unknown_flag
      An argument that is not a flag the command accepts, an abbreviated flag,
      or one-letter aliases written together.
      Next: metais version --help
